translations.text: The Evangelist Luke concluded this day's gospel in few words, but it is filled with the manifold power of the heavenly mystery.
He said, "After eight days were accomplished for the child to be circumcised, his name was called Jesus, which was the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb."
That is, in our language: "After eight days had been fulfilled from the Lord's birth, so that he should be circumcised,
Then his name was called Jesus, that is, Saviour. He had been given that name by the angel before he was conceived in the womb."
Abraham the patriarch was the first man to be circumcised, by God's command. Abraham spoke with God, and God took him into close friendship, more than anyone after Noah's flood, and said to him,
"I am the Almighty Lord; walk before me and be perfect. And I will set my covenant between me and you; and I will multiply you greatly, and you shall be the father of many nations."
Kings will spring from you, and I will set my covenant between me and you, and your offspring after you, that I will be your God and the God of your offspring."
Abraham stretched himself out with all his limbs on the ground, and God said to him, "Keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you, in their generations.
"This is my covenant, which you must keep between me and you: that every male child in your race be circumcised. That will be the sign between me and you.
Every male child, when it is eight nights old, shall be circumcised, both the nobly born and the slave-born; and whoever neglects this, his soul shall perish, because he has made my covenant void.
From now on you shall not be called Abram, but Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
Nor shall your wife be called Sarai, but she shall be called Sarah; and I will bless her, and from her I will give you a son, whom you will call Isaac;
and I will set my covenant with him and with his offspring as an everlasting bond." And after that speech the Almighty went up.
On that same day Abraham was circumcised, and all his household, and afterwards his son Isaac, on the eighth day after his birth.
Abraham's name was at first spelled with five letters, Abram, that is, 'High father';
but God added two letters to his name and called him Abraham, that is, 'Father of many nations', because God said that he would make him the father of many nations.
His wife was called Sarai, which is interpreted 'My lady', but God afterwards called her Sarah, that is, 'Lady', so that she would not be called lady of her own household only, but simply 'Lady';
which is to be understood as the mother of all believing women. Abraham was a hundred years old, and his wife ninety, before they had a child together.
When the child came to them, it came with God's providence and blessing to such a degree that God promised blessing to all mankind through his line.
Abraham's line kept God's covenant ever afterwards; and the leader Moses and the whole nation of Israel all circumcised their children on the eighth day,
and gave them names, until Christ was born in human nature, who instituted baptism and turned the symbolism of the old law into spiritual truth.
It may be that some of you do not know what circumcision is. God commanded Abraham that he and his offspring should keep his covenant;

so that there should be a sign on their bodies as a manifestation that they believed in God; and he commanded that he should take a sharp-edged flint and cut off a part of the skin at the front of his member.
And that sign was then as great among believing people as holy baptism is now, except only that no one could attain the kingdom of God,
before the coming of the one who established the old law, and later, by his presence, turned it to spiritual things:

but all the saints waited in Abraham's dwelling-place without torments, though in hell's punishment, until the Redeemer came, who overpowered the old devil and led his chosen ones to the kingdom of heaven.
The same Saviour, who now cries out awesomely and for our salvation in his gospel,
"Unless a person is born again of water and of the Holy Spirit, he cannot go into the kingdom of heaven," the same Saviour cried out long ago through the old law,
"Whatever male child is not circumcised in the foreskin of his flesh, his soul shall perish, because he has made my covenant void."

This sign remained among God's people until Christ himself came, and he himself was subject to the holy law that he had established, so that he might redeem those who were of necessity subject to the law.
He said that he had not come in order to overthrow the old law, but to fulfil it.
Then on the eighth day after his birth he was circumcised in the flesh, just as he himself had commanded before.
and by that he showed that the old law was holy and good in its time for those who were obedient to it.
It was the custom for the relatives to give the child a name on the eighth day, at the circumcision. But they did not dare to give Christ any other name than the one the archangel had given him
before he was conceived in his mother's womb, that is, Jesus, which in our language is 'Saviour', because he saves his people from their sins.
It is not now permitted to Christian people to keep this circumcision bodily; but nevertheless no one is truly Christian unless he keeps that circumcision in spiritual practices.
What does cutting off the foreskin from the private member signify, except the lessening of lust? This saying might well have been kept hidden from lay people, if it did not have a spiritual meaning.
Unlearned people think it foolish to hear about. But if it seems foolish to anyone, let him quarrel with God, who laid it down, and not with us, who speak of it.
But let everyone know for certain that, unless he diminishes his fleshly desires and lust, he does not keep his Christianity with right observance.
You have often heard about this matter, but your anger is easier for us to bear than the wrath of Almighty God would be if we kept silent about his commandments.
If you will live according to human reason, then you are spiritually circumcised; but if you are subject to your lust, then you are as the prophet said,
"Man, when he was in honour, did not understand it; he is therefore compared to foolish beasts, and has become like them."
For this reason God gave people reason, so that they would know their Creator and earn eternal life by keeping his commandments.
Truly the sinful man is more wretched than any beast, because the beast has no soul, never comes back to life, and does not suffer the punishments to come.
But we who are created in God's likeness, and have an undying soul, shall rise from death and render to God an account of all our thoughts and words and deeds.
Therefore we must not be circumcised in one member only, but we must always diminish foul lust, and turn our eyes away from evil sights, and our ears from evil listening;
[?] our mouth from false speech, our hands from evil deeds, our footsteps from the deadly path, and our hearts from deceit.
If we are circumcised from sins in this way, a new name will be given to us, just as the prophet Isaiah said: "God will call his servants by another name."
The same prophet also said: "You will be called by a new name, which the mouth of God has named." The new name is 'Christianus', that is, Christian.
We are all called Christians after Christ, but we must adorn that honourable name with noble conduct, so that we are not false Christians.
If we keep this spiritual circumcision in our way of life, then we are of Abraham's kin through true faith, just as Paul, the teacher of the nations, said to the faithful,
"If you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise." The apostle Peter also urged faithful women to humility and moderation, saying,
"Just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord, whose daughters you are, doing good and not fearing any trouble."
The eighth day, on which the child was circumcised, signified the eighth age of this world. In that age we will rise from death, freed from all decay and defilement of our body.
The stone knife with which the child was circumcised signified the stone of which the apostle said: "Truly the stone was Christ." He said 'was' because it was a symbol, not because of its substance.
Through faith in Christ, and hope, and true love, devout hearts are continually cleansed from sins by a daily circumcision, and enlightened through his grace.
We have often heard that people call this day New Year's Day, as though this day were the first in the course of the year;
But we find no explanation in Christian books of why this day is counted as the beginning of the year. The ancient Romans, in heathen days, began the year's cycle on this day;
and the Hebrew people at the spring equinox; the Greeks at the summer solstice; and the Egyptian peoples began their reckoning of the year in autumn.
Now our reckoning begins on this day, following the Roman ordinance, not for any divine reason but because of the old custom.

Some of our service-books begin at the Advent of the Lord; yet that is not therefore the beginning of the year, nor is it on this day by any reasoning, although our calendars begin again at this point.
It seems most correct that the beginning of the year should be held on the day on which the Almighty Creator set the sun, the moon, the stars, and the beginning of all times;
that is, on the day on which the Hebrew people begin their count of the year, just as the leader Moses wrote in the books of the law.
for God said to Moses about that month, "This month is the beginning of months, and it shall be the first among the months of the year."
Now the Hebrew people kept the first day of the year at the spring equinox, because on that day the yearly seasons were established.
The eighteenth day of the month that we call March, which you call Hlyda, was the first day of this world.
On that day God made light, and morning, and evening. Then three days went by without measures of time, because the heavenly bodies were not created until the fourth day.
On the fourth day the Almighty set all the heavenly bodies and the seasons of the year, and commanded that they should be signs for days and years.
Now the Hebrews begin their year on the day on which all times were set, that is, on the fourth day of the world's creation;
and the teacher Bede reckons with great reasoning that this day is the twelfth before the Kalends, the day we celebrate in honour of the holy man Benedict for his great merits.
Indeed, the earth also shows by its shoots, which then come to life again, that this time, in which they were created, is the most correct beginning of the year.
Now foolish people practise many kinds of divination on this day, in great error, after heathen custom, contrary to their Christianity,
as if they could prolong their life or their well-being by angering the Almighty Creator.

There are also many caught up in such great error that they regulate their journeys by the moon and their deeds by days, and will not let any of their goods be diminished on Monday, because it is the beginning of the week;
but Monday is not the first of the days of the week; it is the second. Sunday is first in creation, in order, and in honour.
Some foolish men also say that there is a certain kind of livestock which one should not bless, and they say that these animals fare badly through blessing and thrive through cursing,
and so they use God's gift to their own harm, without blessing, with the devil's curse. Every blessing is from God, and cursing from the devil.
God created all creatures, and the devil can create no creature; rather he is an instigator of evil, a worker of falsehood, the originator of sins, and the deceiver of souls.
The creatures that seem hostile were created as a punishment for evil deeds.
Holy men often lived in the wilderness among fierce wolves and lions, among every kind of wild beast and serpent, and nothing could harm them;
rather, they tore apart horned adders with their bare hands and easily killed great dragons, without any harm to themselves, through God's might.
Woe to the man who uses God's creatures without his blessing, with devilish sorceries, when the teacher of the nations, Paul, said,
"Whatever you do in word or in deed, do it always in the Lord's name, giving thanks to the Almighty Father through his Son."

The Christianity of a man who spends his life practising devilish sorceries is worth nothing; he has the outward look of a Christian but is a wretched idolater. As the same apostle said of such people,
"I fear that I laboured in vain when I turned you to God: now you observe days and months with vain sorceries."
Yet, by nature, as it was created, every bodily creature that the earth brings forth is fuller and stronger at the full moon than when the moon is waning.
Trees are the same: if they are felled at the full moon, they are harder and last longer for building, especially if they are worked when the sap is out of them.
This is no sorcery. It is a natural thing, made so at the creation.
The sea, too, follows the moon's course in a wonderful way. The two always go together, in waxing and in waning.
And just as the moon rises four points later each day, so the sea always flows four points later.

Let us set our hope and our happiness on the providence of the Almighty Creator, who ordered all created things in three ways: in measure, in number, and in weight. To him be glory and praise forever and ever. Amen.
